title: Why Earning More Still Keeps You Broke (The Diderot Trap)
alt_title_2: Why High Earners Still Live Paycheck to Paycheck
description_hook: In 1765, French philosopher Denis Diderot got rich overnight—and went broke within months because of one scarlet robe. Here is how the Diderot Effect silently drains modern paychecks and the 72-hour rule to stop it.

scenes.headline: Why Getting a Raise Makes People Poorer
scenes.stat_label: SIX-FIGURE EARNERS LIVING PAYCHECK TO PAYCHECK
bullets: Higher income rarely fixes money stress
A 250-year-old psychological chain reaction explains why
scenes.narration: Sixty-two percent of people earning six figures still live paycheck to paycheck. And a two-hundred-fifty-year-old story explains why.

scenes.headline: Denis Diderot & The Scarlet Robe (1765)
bullets: Gifted one luxury scarlet dressing gown
Suddenly his desk, rug, and chairs looked 'cheap'
scenes.narration: In 1765, philosopher Denis Diderot was gifted a luxurious scarlet robe. Next to that robe, his old wooden desk looked cheap. So he replaced the desk. Then the rug. Then every chair in his home.

scenes.headline: One Upgrade Triggers Five Hidden Costs
scenes.left_body: New phone -> watch -> earbuds -> monthly subscriptions
scenes.right_body: Freeze lifestyle for 12 months after every raise
scenes.narration: Psychologists call this the Diderot Effect. You rarely buy just one upgrade—you buy a whole new identity that demands five more purchases to match.

scenes.headline: The 50% Invisible Raise Rule
scenes.narration: To break the spiral, use the Invisible Raise Rule: whenever your income jumps, automatically route fifty percent into assets before it ever hits your checking account.

scenes.headline: Wealth Is What You Don't Spend
bullets: Wait 72 hours before matching a new purchase
Keep the raise—skip the chain reaction
scenes.narration: Real wealth isn't what people see in your driveway—it's the freedom you didn't trade away. Which is exactly why...
